purpose: Human-reviewed, source-grounded original paraphrases of openly readable scholarly publisher articles. No publisher full-text passages or PDF bytes stored.

articles.title: Prompt-based emotional scaffolding in generative AI: Effects on self-regulated learning and socio-emotional outcomes
articles.license_context: Publisher open-access article; Crossref/OpenAlex record reports CC BY-NC-ND. Only newly written factual paraphrases are recorded, not article text or adapted figures.
articles.method: A preregistered randomized classroom experiment assigned 144 Danish high-school students to standard ChatGPT, an AI chatbot that guided self-regulated learning (SRLbot), or the same approach with emotional support (Emotional SRLbot), with 48 participants in each condition. One learning session lasted about 25 minutes. Tests and surveys were administered before and after, and 85 students completed a four-week follow-up. Interaction traces were coded to examine self-regulatory behaviors.
articles.results: All three groups improved on immediate conceptual-knowledge and learning-transfer tests; however, condition-by-time comparisons were not statistically significant for either outcome (p = .980 and p = .953). At the four-week follow-up, knowledge and transfer change likewise did not differ significantly between groups. Both SRL-based chatbot groups showed larger improvements in enjoyment and reductions in boredom than the general-purpose ChatGPT group. Emotional SRLbot also showed higher task-level performance and reflection indicators in the interaction traces. Hopelessness fell across all groups without a differential treatment effect, and self-efficacy and chatbot trust did not show clear between-group benefits.
articles.discussion: The authors interpret the findings as preliminary support for combining AI prompts about planning, monitoring and reflection with encouragement sensitive to students' emotional states. An intervention that makes learning feel better and increases momentary self-regulatory behavior is not yet evidence of lasting independent learning gains. Theoretical expectations about emotional regulation pathways were not themselves fully tested as causal mediators.
articles.limitations: The intervention lasted only one 25-minute session. The pretest and follow-up knowledge measures had internal consistency below .60, making the learning estimates less reliable. Only 85 of the original 144 returned for follow-up, and dropout related to prior AI experience and initial boredom. Some self-report and trace-based measures diverged, and trace coding was aggregated across each session rather than modeling the sequence of regulatory behaviors. Several outcome comparisons were tested and longer-term effects remain uncertain.

digest.idea: Emotionally responsive AI improved some learning experiences, not measured learning gains over ChatGPT.
digest.explain: In a randomized high-school trial, adding self-regulation prompts and emotional support changed how students felt and engaged during the task, but did not establish superior knowledge or transfer gains.
digest.approach: Preregistered three-arm classroom experiment (144 students; 48 per condition) comparing ChatGPT, an SRL-supporting chatbot and an emotionally supportive SRL chatbot; 85 completed a four-week follow-up.
digest.finding: Tailored agents increased enjoyment and reduced boredom relative to ChatGPT; emotional scaffolding also strengthened observed task-level regulation. Immediate learning gains occurred in all groups, without a statistically significant advantage for the tailored agents.
digest.interpretation: The promise is improved support for moment-to-moment self-regulated work, rather than proof that emotionally responsive AI builds durable independent thinking.
digest.limitation: A single 25-minute intervention, attrition at follow-up, and weak reliability in some knowledge tests limit the learning and retention claims.

articles.review_scope: Original Wiley HTML article, including study methods, results tables and reported limitations; paraphrase and synthesis checked against source. Not an independently replicated analysis.
